text:
Ana (CS): Hey team, Acme reported a regression after today's canary. They say Portuguese (pt-BR) and Arabic translations are returning mixed/incorrect languages and the verbosity changed. Can we triage? @Luca @Sophie
Acme Intl (customer): Hey, we noticed this right after the canary went live ~10:15. Examples below. Previously perfect pt-BR, now we get Spanish fragments + English phrases. Also token count shot up.
Acme Intl (customer): Prompt: \u003cTranslate to Brazilian Portuguese:\u003e 'Please summarize the following policy for customers.'
Acme Intl (customer): Expected: short pt-BR summary. Actual: starts in pt-BR then switches to Spanish mid-sentence, ends with an English note. Sample output:
```
"Resumo: ... então, por favor contacte su representante. Note: see attached link"
```
Acme Intl (customer): For Arabic we see Modern Standard Arabic mixed with Levantine colloquialisms and random english snippets. Bad for UX.
Sophie (Support): Thanks, filing internal ticket. Do you have the request_id or full request payload/logs? Any model name/version the customer saw?
Acme Intl (customer): They hit our prod endpoint: model=redwood-instruct-3.2-canary, route=/v1/generate, content-type JSON. request_id header included: req_0a9f3c. Will DM logs.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout to 10% completed at 2025-11-03T10:12:00Z (deploy id: canary-2025-11-03-02).
Ana (CS): @Luca can you check whether the canary includes the new tokenizer adjustments or a merge that could affect language detection? Also tokenization differences could explain spike in cost.
Luca (ML): I'll pull the canary diff. Quick notes: 1) small change to tokenizer split rules for CJK/punctuation, 2) new language-detection fallback logic meant to avoid empty outputs. Both could interact.
Luca (ML): Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) so we can run locally?
Acme Intl (customer): Repro curl they used:
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-3.2-canary","input":"Translate to pt-BR: Please summarize the new billing policy."}'
```
Sophie (Support): Got it. Will run that against prod and canary traffic mirror. Also asking for the conversation history/previous good request ids to compare tokens.
Luca (ML): Running the repro now against canary and stable in sandbox. Will compare tokenization and logits around the language boundary. If it's LD (lang-detect) fallback, we might see confidence drops and mixed sampling.
Ana (CS): Customer also mentions cost spike — they shared a billing sample where tokens doubled for same prompts. Could be tokenization or prompt appended metadata.
Luca (ML): If token counts doubled, check for accidental prefixing or serialization bug in the canary (e.g., adding system prompts or translated meta). I'll grep the canary for any extra prefill.
Sophie (Support): Quick mitigation: suggest the customer pin to redwood-instruct-3.1-stable until we confirm. Ask if they want us to rollback the canary.
Acme Intl (customer): Pinning is fine for now. We'd prefer no rollback unless needed — can forward more examples.
Luca (ML): Initial sandbox run: canary returns language-mixing on ~60% of runs for the sample; stable returns clean pt-BR. Tokenizer output shows extra invisible tokens inserted before sentence boundaries on canary, causing sampler to flip languages at a BPE boundary. Suspect tokenizer merge table got updated.
Luca (ML): Action items: 1) collect full tokenizer diff between canary and stable, 2) run comprehensive prompt set of ~200 multilingual prompts from Acme, 3) decide rollback if fix cannot be quick.
Ana (CS): I created ticket INF-1429 and attached the customer's examples. Notifying customers of pin advice.
Sophie (Support): I'll draft a customer-facing note: short apology, ask them to pin to 3.1-stable, ask for permission to run their repro across canary logs.
Acme Intl (customer): Thanks, appreciate the quick response. Keep us posted.
Luca (ML): If confirmed tokenizer merge caused it, rollback to 3.1 token table is the fastest fix. If it's language-detect fallback, we may need a fix+retest.
Ana (CS): Updating internal owners: Luca (ML) primary, Sophie (Support) customer comms. Will follow up within 2 business hours with next steps. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
